previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and a history of hepatocellular carcinoma treated with TACE and RFA, was admitted for abdominal pain, vomiting with blood-streaked emesis, and abdominal distension. Evaluation revealed stable vital signs, no active bleeding, and mild acute kidney injury likely due to reduced oral intake. Imaging showed no ascites, bowel obstruction, or new malignancy. Symptoms were attributed to gastritis and portal gastropathy. He improved with supportive care, rehydration, and continuation of home medications. His condition stabilized, and he was discharged home with plans to follow up with Transplant Hepatology and primary care for ongoing management.
problems: Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
Angiodysplasia of intestine (without mention of hemorrhage)
Other specified disorders of stomach and duodenum
Other and unspecified alcohol dependence, in remission

radiology_notes.text:
COMPARISONS:  Liver ultrasound ___.  MRI abdomen ___. 

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale and Doppler ultrasound images were acquired through the
right upper quadrant.

FINDINGS:  The liver is shrunken and nodular, consistent with cirrhosis. 
There is increased echogenicity.  In the right lobe of the liver, there is an
irregular hyperechoic region which measures approximately 2.4 x 1.9 x 2.1 cm. 
This is most consistent with the site of the prior ablation.  Additionally, in
the gallbladder fossa, there is a 1.9 x 1.6 x 1.9 cm hyperechoic rounded
lesion which is unchanged from prior exams, and may be due to post-surgical
changes.  No new lesions are identified, although the examination is limited. 
The main portal vein is patent with normal hepatopetal flow.  There is no
intra- or extra-hepatic biliary duct dilation.  The common bile duct measures
4 mm.  The patient is status post a cholecystectomy.  The spleen is enlarged,
measuring 14.2 cm.  No ascites is identified.  The pancreas is not well
evaluated due to overlying bowel gas.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Nodular cirrhotic liver.
2.  Unchanged hyperechoic foci, consistent with the prior ablation site and
probable post-operative changes after the cholecystectomy.  Evaluation for new
lesions is limited. MRI is more sensitive for surveillance of hepatocellular
carcinoma.
3.  Patent main portal vein.
4.  Stable splenomegaly.
5.  No ascites.

microbiology.comments: NEGATIVE FOR CMV IgM ANTIBODY BY EIA.  INTERPRETATION:  INFECTION AT UNDETERMINED TIME.  A positive IgG result generally indicates past exposure.  Infection with CMV once contracted remains latent and may reactivate when immunity is compromised.  If current infection is suspected, submit follow-up serum in 2-3 weeks.  Greatly elevated serum protein with IgG levels >2000 mg/dl may cause  interference with CMV IgM results.
